This comparison examines the characteristics of pediatric patients with [[ibd|IBD]] who had hospital contact in Denmark between October 1, 2024, and September 30, 2025, dividing them into newly diagnosed patients (182) and prevalent patients with ongoing hospital contact (579) [^src1]. Because the data represents a single reporting period, no longitudinal trends can be established, and the table does not record any specific clinical targets or thresholds to evaluate whether standards were met or missed [^src1].

Across both groups, [[crohns-sygdom|Crohns sygdom]] is the leading diagnosis, accounting for 53% (97 patients) of newly diagnosed cases and 58% (336 patients) of prevalent cases, followed by [[colitis-ulcerosa|Colitis ulcerosa]] at 46% (83) and 42% (243), respectively [^src1]. [[psc|Primær skleroserende kolangitis (PSC)]] is a distant trailer, representing just 1% (2 patients) of new diagnoses and 0% of the prevalent group [^src1]. Demographically, boys lead in both cohorts (60% of new, 54% of prevalent patients), and the vast majority of patients in both groups fall into the 10–17 age bracket (89% of new, 94% of prevalent) [^src1]. The 0–1 age group is the absolute trailer, comprising only 2% (4 patients) of new diagnoses and 0% of prevalent cases [^src1]. 

In terms of healthcare utilization, both groups average 15 contacts per patient, though newly diagnosed patients have a slightly higher median of 14 contacts compared to 13 for prevalent patients [^src1]. Physical consultations are the dominant contact type, making up 64% (1,103 contacts) for newly diagnosed patients and 69% (3,933 contacts) for the prevalent group, while virtual contacts trail at 36% and 31%, respectively [^src1].

Summary: Tabellen sammenligner karakteristika for nydiagnosticerede og prævalente børn med IBD, og viser at begge grupper domineres af Crohns sygdom, drenge og aldersgruppen 10–17 år, samt at fysisk kontakt udgør størstedelen af kontakterne.
